title: トランプ氏にNOと言わぬ日本、家康もぼやいた同盟の「実利と忍耐」
extracted_text:
「トランプ米大統領にノーと言えない日本」。こう題した英フィナンシャル・タイムズ（FT）の10日付の記事が話題を集めた。日本は対米依存に代わる選択肢がなくつらい立場にある、と指摘した内容だ。

トランプ米政権は同盟国に高圧的な姿勢を示す。西欧の首脳は公然と米国に不満を表明し、核戦力を含め自主防衛力の強化にも動く。日本とは対照的だ。

高市早苗首相は3月の日米首脳会談で「世界中に平和と繁栄をもたらせるのはドナルドだけだ」と持ち上げた。約束した対米投資5500億ドルの案件も積み上げた。

「こびた」という批判がある一方で、日本国内の世論調査では首脳会談を評価する割合が高かった。機先を制してトランプ氏からの無理な要求を封じたとして肯定的に受け止められた。

政府の同行者の一人は「中東情勢に関心が集まったが、会談の狙いは対中国だ。所期の目的を達成できた」と話す。5月に予定する米中首脳会談について「貿易でディール（取引）はあるかもしれないが、米国は台湾など安全保障で譲歩しない」との感触を得たと明かす。

現在の日米同盟は中国抑止の意義が大きい。トランプ氏の機嫌を損なわず、対中姿勢で足並みがそろえば日本には合格点だ。

トランプ氏が2期目で最初に対面した外国首脳はイスラエルのネタニヤフ首相だった。その次は当時の石破茂首相だ。米国も対中戦略で欠かせない日本を重視する。

防衛研究所の飯田将史氏は「米国の政治家や研究者と意見を交わすと、中国の覇権を許さないという強い意志を感じる」と語る。

同氏は欧州が対峙するロシアを「ディクライニング・パワー（斜陽の大国）」とみなす。「米国は欧州だけでロシアを抑止できるのではないかとみている」と分析する。米国が日欧への対応に差をつける背景だという。

古今東西、長く継続する同盟には利害の一致がある。16世紀の戦国時代、三河を領国とした徳川家康は西隣の織田信長と同盟を結んだ。

家康にとって東方の武田や今川などの脅威に備えるため同盟に合理性があった。織田は北の美濃や西の京をめざし、家康に東側の防波堤の役割を期待した。

力関係は信長が優位だった。家康は理不尽な要求に耐えた。遠い近江・姉川に自ら出兵し、敵国への内通を疑われた妻子の命も奪わざるを得なかった。

歴史家の磯田道史氏は著書「徳川家康　弱者の戦略」でこんな記録を紹介している。家康は「いったん信玄についた後、それを裏切って信長に属していたらもっと優遇されたかもしれない」とぼやいた。

家康も信長に自らの価値を理解させるのに苦労した。それでも感情を抑え、関係の維持に汗をかいたはずだ。信長は最後まで同盟の必要性を見失わなかった。

いまの日本も米国の要求に苦しみながら、自らの役割を認識して同盟維持に努力する。22年末に防衛政策を転換し、長射程ミサイルを保有した。26年には安保3文書を改定し、防衛費をさらに増やす大事が控える。

24年、岸田文雄首相は米議会の演説でこう訴えた。「米国は独りではない。日本は米国と共にある」。岸田氏は山岡荘八著「徳川家康」を読んでいる。

青年期に「律義者」と言われた家康は老年期に一転して謀略を駆使した。環境に応じて戦略は変える必要がある。いまの国際環境下の日本で能動的に「ノー」と言わないのはリアリズムだ。問題はそこに確固たる戦略があるかどうかだ。

（秋山裕之）

translated_text:
"Japan that cannot say no to President Trump." An article with this title in the British Financial Times (FT) dated the 10th has gathered attention. It points out that Japan is in a difficult position with no alternative to depending on the US.

The Trump administration takes a high-handed approach toward allies. Western European leaders openly express dissatisfaction with the US and are moving to strengthen their self-defense capabilities, including nuclear forces. This is in contrast to Japan.

Prime Minister Kōno Eisake boosted Trump at the Japan-US summit in March, saying " Donald is the only one who can bring peace and prosperity to the world." Investment commitments worth $550 billion were added to the agenda.

While there is criticism of being overly subservient, domestic opinion polls in Japan showed high approval for the summit. It was viewed positively as having preemptively blockaded unreasonable demands from Trump.

One government official who accompanied the delegation said, "While attention was focused on the Middle East situation, the purpose of the summit was China. We achieved our intended objective." Regarding the US-China summit planned for May, they expressed the sense that "there may be a trade deal, but the US will not make concessions on security matters such as Taiwan."

The current US-Japan alliance holds significant value for containing China. If Japan doesn't anger Trump and maintains alignment on China policy, it passes muster.

The first foreign leader Trump met face-to-face in his second term was Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu. The next was then-Prime Minister Shimpō Ishiba. The US also values Japan as indispensable to its China strategy.

Defense Research Institute researcher Masashi Iida says, "When exchanging views with US politicians and researchers, I feel a strong determination not to allow Chinese hegemony."
He views Europe as viewing Russia as a "declining power." "The US seems to think Europe alone can contain Russia," he analyzes. This is the background behind the US making distinctions between its approach to Japan and Europe.

Throughout history, long-lasting alliances have aligned interests. In the 16th century during the Warring States period, Tokugawa Ieyasu, who ruled Mikawa, formed an alliance with his western neighbor Oda Nobunaga.

For Ieyasu, the alliance made sense to prepare against threats from eastern forces like the Takeda and Imagawa. Nobunaga aimed north toward Mino and west toward Kyoto, expecting Ieyasu to serve as a buffer on the eastern side.

The power dynamic had Nobunaga in the stronger position. Ieyasu endured unreasonable demands. He personally led troops to the distant Anegawa in Ōmi, and had to take the lives of his own wife and child who were suspected of collusion with the enemy.

Historian Tsutomu Isoda introduces such records in his book "Tokugawa Ieyasu: The Strategy of the Weak." Ieyasu complained, "After initially siding with Takeda, if I had betrayed that and remained loyal to Nobunaga, I might have been treated even better."

Ieyasu also struggled to make Nobunaga understand his value. Even so, he must have suppressed his emotions and worked hard to maintain the relationship. Nobunaga never lost sight of the alliance's necessity until the end.

Modern Japan also suffers from US demands while recognizing its role and making efforts to maintain the alliance. At the end of 2022, Japan shifted its defense policy and acquired long-range missiles. In 2026, revising the three security documents and further increasing defense spending awaits.

In 2024, Prime Minister Kishida Fumiko appealed in a speech to the US Congress: " America is not alone. Japan is with America." Kishida has read Tokugawa Ieyasu by Yamaoka Sōhachi.

Ieyasu, called "a man of integrity" in his youth, later turned to using stratagems. Strategies need to change according to the environment. In today's international environment, actively not saying "no" in Japan is realism. The question is whether there is a solid strategy behind it.
title_en: Japan That Can't Say NO to Trump, Where Ieyasu Also Grumbled About Alliance's 'Practical Benefits and Patience'
